newsitem.title: UK: Contractors say Eurotunnel loses big claim.
newsitem.headline: Contractors say Eurotunnel loses big claim.

text.p: Debt-laden Eurotunnel SA/Plc saw its hopes fade Tuesday of getting the firms that built the Anglo-French subsea railway to help to dig it out of its deep financial hole.

The Transmanche Link (TML) consortium of tunnel contractors said that a "Panel of Experts" appointed to arbitrate disputes with Eurotunnel had rejected the bulk of a 1 billion pound ($1.6 billion) claim made by Eurotunnel against TML.

Eurotunnel's claim was submitted to the panel in December 1995. It alleged delays in deliveries and inadequacies in rolling stock supplied by TML for its Le Shuttle train service between Folkestone, England, and Calais, France.

"The Panel's decision does not recognise any merit in the majority of Eurotunnel's claims and they were rejected on both legal and factual grounds," TML said in a statement commenting on the panel's 146-page judgment.
"TML takes the view, therefore, that Eurotunnel's 1 billion pounds claim is nullified by the Panel's ruling."
The statement was released on behalf of TML by consortium member Tarmac Plc .

In its own response to the judgment Eurotunnel said that the panel had decided the company was entitled to damages for deficiencies in some rolling stock supplied, but rejected claims for loss of revenue.
